subject: Request: short-term capacity bridge for Brightlane launch
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightlane.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: 2025-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Short-term capacity request — upcoming promo spike

Hi Sean,

Quick one — we have a marketing promo kicking off on June 18 that will generate a short, sharp traffic spike (estimated peak ~3.2M tokens over 48 hours). Our infra team asked whether Redwood can provide a provisional quota expansion for 72 hours to avoid throttling during the launch.

Attached is a short worksheet with our expected QPS/seq-length profile (Brightlane_QoS_Request.xlsx). Two questions:

- Can you temporarily raise our soft threshold for the 18th–20th window?
- How will we be billed for any overrun tokens during that provisional window?

We’re happy to sign a one-off addendum/PO if needed — procurement is looped on cc. Appreciate a quick sketch of the commercial path and any docs we should sign.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product Ops
Brightlane

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-15T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity request — upcoming promo spike

Alyssa — thanks for the worksheet, that’s helpful. TL;DR: we can support a short provisional uplift with a clear true-up and a capped surcharge. Proposed path below.

Proposal (short-term bridge, 72h):
- Provisional soft threshold increase to cover the 48–72h surge window (one-time enablement).
- Billing: overrun tokens during the uplift will be billed at your current unit rates, prorated to the actual window, plus a 5% short-term facility surcharge to cover burst provisioning.
- If you convert the uplift into a recurring higher commit within 30 days, we’ll credit the 5% surcharge back against the first invoice of the new commit.
- Requirement: we need a PO or signed short-term addendum (Redwood-short-term-addendum.docx). If procurement provides a PO reference by EOD tomorrow we can lock the change.

Operational notes:
- To avoid surprises we’ll enable prefix caching and a tighter batching cap for the window; this usually reduces billed tokens by ~6–9% for these traffic shapes.
- If you expect >3.5M tokens peak or sustained >3 min p99 latency, tell us now so we can provision headroom rather than a provisional lift.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the exact start/end times for the 72h window (we’ve tentatively set 2025-06-18 00:00 UTC — please confirm).
2) Procurement to send PO or sign the addendum.
3) I’ll drop the provisional rate sheet (attached) and Ben will share the invoice sample.

I’ll leave Ben and Marissa on thread for the PO/invoice follow-up.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightlane.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-15T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term capacity request — upcoming promo spike

Thanks Sean — that approach sounds reasonable. A couple clarifying items from procurement:

- Can you confirm the SLA during the provisional window? We need an acknowledgement of target p95 latency and an incident contact.
- For the credit of the 5% surcharge, what qualifies as converting to a "recurring higher commit"? (min. commit size and timing)
- Proc also asks for a sample invoice so they know how the prorated line will appear.

Procurement will attempt to issue a PO by EOD tomorrow — they’re asking for the addendum to include the PO# field. I’ve attached the worksheet we sent earlier.

On timing: start can be 2025-06-18T00:00Z and run until 2025-06-20T23:59Z if that’s easiest for you.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — will confirm PO once received.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product Ops, Brightlane

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightlane.com>, procurement@brightlane.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Short-term capacity request — upcoming promo spike (action items + sample invoice)

Hi Alyssa / procurement team — following up with the specific asks.

1) SLA / contacts: during the provisional uplift we’ll maintain our standard production SLOs (p95 token latency target 350ms on the hosted tier). For the 72h window we’ll designate an incident on-call: oncall@redwood.ai plus direct escalation to me if you see material degradation.

2) Commit conversion credit: converting means signing a 3-month or longer reserved commit at or above 20% higher monthly token commit vs your current baseline within 30 days of the uplift window close. If you meet that, the 5% surcharge charged on the provisional window will be applied as a credit on the first invoice of the new commit term. We’ll include the exact language in the addendum.

3) Sample invoice: attached is an example line item showing the prorated uplift and surcharge (Redwood-provisional-rate-sheet.pdf). The bill will show: base usage (normal), uplift window overrun (token count), uplift surcharge (5%), and any credits applied later.

Attachment summary: Redwood-provisional-rate-sheet.pdf (pricing breakout), Redwood-short-term-addendum.docx (legal addendum template).

If procurement sends PO# by EOD we’ll schedule the enablement for 2025-06-18T00:00Z. If anything looks off on the invoice sample let me know and we’ll adjust formatting for your AP process.

Action items:
- Procurement: send PO# referencing addendum template OR sign and return the addendum.
- Alyssa: confirm the final start/end UTC window if different from proposed.
- Sean/Marissa: we’ll hit the toggle once PO/addendum is received.

Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
